title: kith-core: Role and Identity types
description:
What: Define Role enum and Identity struct in src/auth.rs.

Module file: crates/kith-core/src/auth.rs — create this file, then add 'pub mod auth;' to src/lib.rs.

Algorithm:
1. Define Role enum with variants Owner and Peer.
   Serde: rename_all = "lowercase".
   Derives: Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize.
2. Define Identity struct:
   user_id: String  (opaque Tailscale UserProfile.ID — never parse)
   login_name: String  (email-shaped or bare, may be empty on Headscale)
   display_name: Option<String>  (may be absent)
   Derives: Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize.
3. Add a comment on user_id: '// Opaque stable key. Never parse. Compare with == only.'
4. Add a method: impl Identity { pub fn display(&self) -> &str { ... } }
   Returns: display_name if Some and non-empty, else login_name if non-empty, else user_id.
5. Add 'pub mod auth;' to src/lib.rs.
6. Run: cargo check -p kith-core

Defensive programming rules:
- Never add a method that parses user_id as email, UUID, or any structured format
- display() method must never return empty string (always falls back to user_id)
- No unwrap() in the display() method

Tests (independent oracle: test vectors manually constructed):
- Role serialization: assert Role::Owner serializes to "owner", Role::Peer to "peer"
- Identity.display(): test all three fallback cases (display_name present, absent/empty with login_name, both absent)
- Round-trip: serialize/deserialize Identity, assert field equality
